matt-furniss.name: Matt Furniss
matt-furniss.bio: Matt Furniss is an English composer and sound designer who began professional game-audio work as a teenager. He worked at Krisalis and on a large number of computer and console conversions, with C64 credits in the CCG archive including Chase H.Q., Klax and Escape from the Planet of the Robot Monsters.

matt-gray.name: Matt Gray
matt-gray.bio: Matt Gray is an English producer and composer best known in game-music circles for his Commodore 64 work. His soundtrack for Last Ninja 2 is among his most recognised game scores, and he has remained connected with C64 music through later recordings and reworkings of his catalogue.

matthew-cannon.name: Matthew Cannon
matthew-cannon.bio: Matthew Cannon is an English composer and sound programmer who joined Ocean while still in his teens. His home-computer work includes music for licensed games and arcade conversions, with CCG-linked credits including Batman: The Movie, Nightbreed, The Untouchables and Civilization.

michael-z-land.name: Michael Land
michael-z-land.bio: Michael Land is an American composer and audio programmer best known for his work at Lucasfilm Games and LucasArts. He wrote the defining music for The Secret of Monkey Island and, with Peter McConnell, developed the iMUSE interactive music system that became central to many LucasArts adventures.

nation-12.name: Nation 12
nation-12.bio: Nation 12 was a British electronic music project associated with John Foxx and collaborators from the late-1980s and early-1990s dance-music scene. The group contributed music used in Bitmap Brothers games including Speedball 2: Brutal Deluxe and Gods, giving the project an enduring connection with Amiga game music.

neil-brennan.name: Neil Brennan
neil-brennan.bio: Neil Brennan is a musician, composer and programmer associated with Melbourne House and Beam Software. He became the company's principal C64 musician, built sound tools and a music language around the SID chip, and later adapted that system for Nintendo hardware; his CCG credits include The Way of the Exploding Fist, Fist II, Judge Dredd and Samurai Warrior.

nick-scarim.name: Nick Scarim
nick-scarim.bio: Nick Scarim is an American composer whose game credits include the Commodore 64 Spy vs Spy series. His later audio work also extended into television and children's media, while the CCG archive records his music on all three early Spy vs Spy computer games.

olof-gustafsson.name: Olof Gustafsson
olof-gustafsson.bio: Olof Gustafsson is a Swedish composer and programmer who emerged from the demoscene before becoming a co-founder of Digital Illusions. His Amiga work includes music for Pinball Dreams and Benefactor, and his later career continued through games, technology and independent music projects.

paul-butler.name: Paul Butler
paul-butler.bio: Paul Butler is a Canadian game designer, programmer and musician who co-founded Artech Digital Productions in Ottawa in 1982. His C64 music credits in the CCG archive include Ace of Aces, Apollo 18 and The Train: Escape to Normandy, alongside wider design and production work.

paul-clansey.name: Paul Clansey
paul-clansey.bio: Paul Clansey is a British game developer and musician from the early home-computer period. The CCG archive links him to Alien and Give My Regards to Broad Street on the C64, while surviving interviews also document his programming and development work on other projects.

paul-hodgson.name: Paul Hodgson
paul-hodgson.bio: Paul Hodgson is a British C64-era musician whose recorded game credits include Super Pipeline, Bozo's Night Out, Gyropod, Poster Paster and Uchi Mata. Public biographical information is limited, so the profile concentrates on his verified game work.

paul-norman.name: Paul Norman
paul-norman.bio: Paul Norman is an American musician, programmer and game designer who became closely associated with Cosmi's Commodore 64 releases. He combined programming, game design and original audio on titles including Forbidden Forest, Beyond the Forbidden Forest and Aztec Challenge.
